Both-states control audit of the program's detector surface. 17 detectors, 18 paired probes (known-BROKEN fixture must fire; known-GOOD twin must stay silent). Result: 17 VALID, 1 DECORATIVE. Artifact is 53,418 bytes and passes `receipt_schema_gate.py --schema-only` -> SCHEMA-VALID:ADV-0009.

META-CONTROL PASSED (the unit's own calibration case). The one DECORATIVE detector is exactly the one the spec named as known-disarmed: validate.py's V-FIELDS under the invocation CI actually uses. Deleting the ENTIRE `defaults` block from the catalog and running `python tools/command-center/validate.py` bare gives exit 0 + `SUCCESS:cc-validate` -- while the SAME run prints `work_unit_fields_unresolved=1133` in its own stats line. The tool measures the breakage and declines to report it. Three mechanically independent signals: (1) exit code, (2) the tool's own printed stat, (3) a static scan of quality.yml showing the only non-comment invocation is `python tools/command-center/validate.py` with `--require-complete` on zero invocations. D02 proves the CHECK is sound -- same fixture + `--require-complete` -> exit 1, 1,133 V-FIELDS violations. The defect is the missing flag in CI (quality.yml:402), not the rule (validate.py:85 default, :272 guard).

Zero FALSE-POSITIVE-MACHINEs found.

INCIDENTAL DEFECT (P2, not a both-states failure): `platform/lib/receipt_schema_gate.py` crashes with an unhandled `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable` at `retry.get("attempts", [])` on ADV-0003, whose `retry.attempts` is the scalar `1`. The same file under `--schema-only` reports 14 clean schema errors, so the schema layer CAN diagnose it -- the full path reaches predicate code first and dies. It still fails closed (exit non-zero), so it is a diagnosability defect, not silence.

Also observed: all 14 sibling ADV-* receipts are rejected by the schema gate (14/14 exit 1). That is evidence the gate discriminates against the live corpus, NOT a verdict on those receipts' quality -- several are deliberate counterexample fixtures. No claim offered there.

Artifact `state` is BLOCKED, not SUCCESS. Measurement is complete and no verdict is downgraded; the receipt schema's SUCCESS branch additionally requires condition 9 (independent reviewer -- the unit demands two from different vendors; none ran) and condition 11 (manifest registration -- the spawn contract forbids editing shared files). Asserting either would be the exact fabrication this unit exists to detect, so both are reported false. Per the unit's own completion_sentinel the delivery conditions are all met.

result.control_fired:
Two layers, both executed.

1. THE UNIT'S MANDATED META-CONTROL. validate.py V-FIELDS with require_complete defaulting to False, invoked bare as CI invokes it, had to be classified silent-in-both -- "if the audit passes that one, the audit itself is broken." Measured good exit 0 / bad exit 0 -> DECORATIVE. The audit did NOT pass it. Corroborated three ways (exit code, the tool's own `work_unit_fields_unresolved=1133` stat, and the workflow-invocation scan finding zero `--require-complete`), so the reading is not a single-signal artifact.

2. THREE-WAY CALIBRATION OF THE AUDIT'S OWN CLASSIFIER, run against synthetic detectors whose true label is known by construction: always-exit-0 -> DECORATIVE (ok); always-exit-1 -> FALSE-POSITIVE-MACHINE (ok); exit-by-input -> VALID (ok). 3/3. This proves the classifier is not constant in ANY direction -- a matcher that only ever emits VALID would have scored 1/3.

THREE HARNESS DEFECTS WERE CAUGHT BEFORE BECOMING FINDINGS (recorded in report.harness_defects_caught, and the reason retry.count=2):
- D10 first read "fires in BOTH states" -> would have been reported as a false-positive machine. Cause: my GOOD fixture had 60 tracked .json, below jsonparse's OWN fail-closed floor of 800, so its floor fired on the good state. 900 files -> (0,1) VALID.
- D08 first read exit 2 ("can't open file" -- not a detector reading at all), then "fires in both" from a 1-reference fixture below refcheck's own floor of 12. 15 references -> (0,1) VALID.
- D13 first read "silent in BOTH states" -> would have been a fabricated second DECORATIVE finding. Cause: my rival defined `reduce_claims`/`ClaimState`, which are NOT in reducer.py's BANNED_DEFINITIONS = {evaluate, CONDITIONS, CONDITION_TEXT, NON_WAIVABLE}. A rival defining CONDITIONS/NON_WAIVABLE/evaluate was caught at rival.py:3 -> (0,1) VALID.

Lesson recorded in the artifact: a GOOD fixture below a tool's own fail-closed floor manufactures a false "fires-in-both", and a plausible-looking broken fixture is not a broken fixture -- derive it from the detector's own rule table.

Self-hash honesty: an earlier draft declared a stale real SHA-256 from the previous write iteration (a file cannot contain its own hash). That was a false measurement of exactly the class this unit audits; it was corrected to a documented CANONICAL-FORM hash (the file with artifacts[0].sha256 set to 64 zeros), which was then independently recomputed off the written bytes and matched. `bytes` is the literal on-disk size and matches stat (53,418).
